newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota crops receive warmth, but rain needed.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota crops receive warmth, but rain needed.

text.p: A long-awaited week of seasonably warm temperatures accelerated plant growth and made most fields look better during the week ended Sunday, according to the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service.
Rain was spotty and light and crops need more moisture soon, the report said.
The condition of spring wheat improved slightly to 80 percent good to excellent, up from 76 percent a week earlier. Spring wheat was 97 percent planted as of Sunday, up from 91 percent a week ago.

Corn was 97 percent emgerged, up from 80 percent a week ago, 84 a year ago and the five-year average of 86 percent. Corn was rated 52 percent good to excellent, 39 percent fair, eight percent poor and one percent very poor.
Soybeans were 78 percent emerged, up from 31 percent last week, 46 percent last year and the five-year average of 62 percent.
Topsoil moisture as of Friday was rated two percent surplus, 52 percent adequate, 29 percent short and 17 percent very short.
